"**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.

According to Nielsen Media Research who measure the number of minutes watched by United States audiences on television sets, *Moon Knight* was the third-most watched original series across streaming services for the week of April 11–17 with 638 million minutes watched,[23] which was a 5% increase from the previous week.[24] According to streaming aggregator Reelgood, which looks at viewing figures on streaming services in the United States and United Kingdom, *Moon Knight* was the most-watched series for the week ending April 15, 2022.[25] *Moon Knight* was the top streaming series for viewers in the United States for the week ending April 17 according to Whip Media's TV Time.[26]



### Critical response

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

"**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.


</fragment>
</document>

<fragment>

"**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.

According to Nielsen Media Research who measure the number of minutes watched by United States audiences on television sets, *Moon Knight* was the third-most watched original series across streaming services for the week of April 11–17 with 638 million minutes watched,[23] which was a 5% increase from the previous week.[24] According to streaming aggregator Reelgood, which looks at viewing figures on streaming services in the United States and United Kingdom, *Moon Knight* was the most-watched series for the week ending April 15, 2022.[25] *Moon Knight* was the top streaming series for viewers in the United States for the week ending April 17 according to Whip Media's TV Time.[26]

<fragment>

"**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.

## Release

[edit]

*Moon Knight* debuted on Disney+ on March 30, 2022.[144] It consists of six episodes,[54] releasing weekly until May 4.[145] A special screening occurred on March 16 at Cine Capitol in Madrid,[146] and on March 17 at the British Museum in London,[147] with the red carpet premiere on March 22 at El Capitan Theatre in Los Angeles.[148][149] It is part of Phase Four of the MCU.[150]



## Reception

[edit]

### Audience viewership

[edit]

Parrot Analytics, which looks at consumer engagement in consumer research, streaming, downloads, and on social media, reported that *Moon Knight* had the most in-demand United States series premiere in the first quarter of 2022. It had 33.4 times the average demand of all other series in the U.S. during its first 30 days.[151]

***Moon Knight*** is an American television miniseries created by Jeremy Slater for the streaming service Disney+, based on the Marvel Comics featuring the character of the same name. It is the sixth television series in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) to be produced by Marvel Studios, sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It follows Marc Spector and Steven Grant, two alters of a man with dissociative identity disorder (DID), as they are drawn into a mystery involving Egyptian gods. Slater serves as head writer with Mohamed Diab leading the directing team.

"**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.

## Moon Knight Episodes - Season 1

1. **"The Goldfish Problem"** - Episode 1
   - Written by Jeremy Slater, directed by Mohamed Diab
   - Introduces Steven Grant/Marc Spector and his dissociative identity disorder

2. **"Summon the Suit"** - Episode 2
   - Written by Beau DeMayo, directed by Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead
   - Steven discovers he can summon the Moon Knight suit

3. **"The Friendly Type"** - Episode 3
   - Written by Michael Kastelein & Peter Cameron, directed by Mohamed Diab
   - Features the appearance of Arthur Harrow and reveals more about the Egyptian mythology

4. **"The Tomb"** - Episode 4
   - Written by Alex Meenehan & Sabir Pirzada, directed by Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead
   - An adventure episode with Indiana Jones-style tomb exploration

5. **"Asylum"** - Episode 5
   - Written by Rebecca Kirsch & Matthew Orton, directed by Mohamed Diab
   - A psychological hospital episode that reveals deeper truths about Marc's past

6. **"Gods and Monsters"** - Episode 6 (Finale)
   - Written by Jeremy Slater, directed by Mohamed Diab
   - The season finale featuring the confrontation with Ammit and the reveal of Jake Lockley

The series starred Oscar Isaac as Marc Spector/Steven Grant/Jake Lockley, along with May Calamawy as Layla El-Faouly/Scarlet Scarab and Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. The show was praised for its unique psychological approach to the superhero genre and its exploration of Egyptian mythology and mental health themes.

The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. "**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.

"**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.

It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.

***The Futon Critic*** is a website that provides articles and information regarding prime time programming on broadcast and cable networks in the United States. The site publishes reviews of prime time programming and interviews of people in the television industry, as well as republishing Nielsen ratings data reports and press releases provided by television networks. *The Futon Critic* was founded by Brian Ford Sullivan in 1997.



## History

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
Brian Ford Sullivan, CEO of Futon Media, registered *The Futon Critic* on January 14, 1997.[1][2] From its founding, the site has published reviews on prime time programming, as well as interviews its staff conducted with members of the television industry.[3] The site also contains sections of articles dedicated to republishing press releases, network schedules and Nielsen ratings data, which have been cited by articles on websites such as *The Huffington Post* and TV by the Numbers.[4][5][6] Its publications of Nielsen ratings data have also been used as a resource by institutions such as the University of Colorado Boulder and Temple University.[7][8]

"**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.

"**The Friendly Type**" is the third episode of the American television miniseries *Moon Knight*, based on Marvel Comics featuring the character Moon Knight. It follows Marc Spector as he returns to Egypt to find Ammit's tomb before Arthur Harrow does. The episode is set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), sharing continuity with the films of the franchise. It was written by Beau DeMayo and Peter Cameron & Sabir Pirzada and directed by Mohamed Diab.


Oscar Isaac stars as Marc Spector / Moon Knight and Steven Grant / Mr. Knight alongside Ethan Hawke as Arthur Harrow. May Calamawy, Khalid Abdalla, Ann Akinjirin, David Ganly, Karim El-Hakim, F. Murray Abraham, and Gaspard Ulliel also star. Diab joined the series by October 2020 to direct four episodes. Filming took place at Origo Studios in Budapest, with location filming occurring in Jordan.
